quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What about the front brake?

options.text: Use it only when you need to stop quickly.
Use it only on slippery roads.
It is not as strong as the rear brake.
It is safe to use if you use it correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use if you use it correctly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake, and it is safe to use when you use it properly.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them tightly or place them in saddlebags. Putting loads high on the back of the seat can raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and throw off your balance. Always spread loads equally on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles, just a few minutes after a rider starts out.

questions.question: How should you look through a turn?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to see better.
Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn just your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What should you do if you are riding next to another vehicle?

options.text: Stay alongside the vehicle until the next exit.
Let the other driver handle it.

questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in the vehicle's blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape route if a hazard appears. If you are riding next to another vehicle, speed up or drop back.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride over an obstacle?

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Stay on your seat and lift your feet off the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep your motorcycle upright. Just before hitting it, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps you be seen the most?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors when riding. Bright orange, yellow, red, or green are best. Avoid drab or dark colors.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when another vehicle is passing you?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
On the left side of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.
Move between all three parts of the lane as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the side closer to the passing vehicle increases your risk of a crash. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to move back into your lane too early.

questions.question: What should you do before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time?

options.text: Practice riding on an empty road.
Flash your lights so others see you.
Practice riding on the road's shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on an empty road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger or heavy load in traffic for the first time, practice on a quiet road. This lets you get used to how your motorcycle handles the extra weight.

questions.question: When will a helmet NOT give the best protection?

options.text: If it is certified by the DOT.
If it is free of defects.

questions.explanation: A helmet should meet U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and be free of cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps for maximum protection.

questions.question: If your motorcycle chain or belt breaks, what will happen?

options.text: The rear wheel will suddenly get more power.
The rear wheel will suddenly lose power.
The front wheel will suddenly lose power.
The front wheel will suddenly get more power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rear wheel will suddenly lose power.
questions.explanation: If your drive chain or belt breaks, power to the rear wheel will stop immediately.

questions.question: What should you do to stop quickly?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off the road and wait for the rain to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Do not ride down the center of the lane in wet conditions. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is usually best, but this can change depending on traffic and conditions.

questions.question: How should you swerve?

options.text: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, push gently on the handgrip on the side where you want to go. To swerve left, push the left handgrip, then push the right to straighten out. To swerve right, push the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe motorcycle riders should wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to feel effects?
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to ride. Riding a motorcycle while under the influence is both illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: The body removes about one drink per hour. If someone had eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.explanation: To find how many drinks remain, subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. In this case, eight drinks minus four hours equals about four drinks left.

questions.question: What following distance should you normally keep?
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, what can happen?

options.text: The motorcycle may jolt forward and the rear tire could skid.
The motorcycle may accelerate too quickly.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle may jolt forward and the rear tire could skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear without going slowly enough, the motorcycle will jolt and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Approach it slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach it slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. If a dog is chasing you, downshift and ride slowly toward it. Then speed up and ride away from it.

questions.question: What can goggles protect?

options.text: Your face but not your eyes.
Your eyes but not your face.
Neither your face nor your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your eyes but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes. Only a face shield can protect your entire face in a crash.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: How do you brake hardest in a straight line?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use both front and rear brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: The hardest braking happens when you use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.

questions.question: What can long-term wind noise exposure do to you?

options.text: It is safer than listening to music.

questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Use hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Give you a good view of the shoulder.
Give you a poor view of road hazards.
Invite others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: Choose your lane position so you can see others and they can see you. Don't stay in another driver's blind spot.

questions.question: Which brakes should you use when slowing or stopping?

options.text: Either the front or rear brake, not both.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to travel ______ than they actually do.
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles look farther away and seem slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their real location and speed.

questions.question: When a motorcycle group passes another vehicle, what should they do?

options.text: Let one rider finish passing before the next rider starts.
Let several riders pass at the same time.
Have the last rider wave to signal no more motorcycles are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let one rider finish passing before the next rider starts.
questions.explanation: Group riders should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish their pass and return to formation before the next rider begins to pass.

questions.question: A person drinks 7 alcoholic drinks over 3 hours. The body removes about 1 drink per hour. How many drinks remain 3 hours after the last drink?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. After 7 drinks in 3 hours, plus 3 more hours passing, 6 drinks are removed. Four drinks remain.

questions.question: Without a helmet, how much more likely is a rider to suffer a critical head injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: Without a helmet, a rider is five times more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Guarantees that they will yield to you.
Doesn't mean that they see you.
Is not worth the effort it takes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doesn't mean that they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact. A driver may look directly at you but still not notice you. Never assume that eye contact means they will yield to you.

questions.question: To lower the chance of a crash, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Be prepared to react to hazards.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others. Signal your intentions clearly. Keep safe distance from other vehicles. Watch ahead for hazards and be ready to react. Never rely on hoping drivers will see you.

questions.question: Impairment from alcohol:

options.text: Begins at about half of the legal limit.
Occurs only if you have had multiple drinks.

questions.explanation: Even one drink affects your ability to ride safely. You can be impaired well below the legal limit. Do not drink any alcohol before riding.

questions.question: Where is the greatest potential for conflict between motorcycle operators and other drivers?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcyclists and other drivers. Use extra caution when approaching and crossing intersections.

questions.question: In a normal turn:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Provide you with an escape route.
Welcome other drivers into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Welcome other drivers into your lane.
questions.explanation: Choose your lane position to stay out of blind spots, be seen better, avoid road hazards, and have an escape route. Position yourself to discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Not use any brakes, but downshift.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and avoid sudden moves. Use both brakes when you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: To stop quickly, it is best to:

options.text: Throttle down and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When conducting a pre-ride check, be sure that:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes cause some friction with the steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check each brake lever separately. Make sure each one feels firm and can hold the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Should be avoided because they will distract you.
Should be avoided since other drivers will see you easily.
Are only recommended in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often. Knowing what is behind you is important for your safety. Make frequent mirror checks part of your regular scanning routine.

questions.question: How do you operate the gearshift lever on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: When should a motorcyclist shift gears?

options.text: While making sudden power changes in a turn.
While using the brake throughout the turn.

questions.explanation: You should change gears before you enter a turn, not during it.

questions.question: What type of sign is usually rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. These signs tell you the traffic rules you must follow.

questions.question: What should you do to stop quickly?

options.text: Use the rear brake firmly and slowly increase the front brake pressure.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What should you NOT check before riding your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Check your tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn before every ride. You do not need to check the paint.

questions.question: What should you do if another vehicle is following you too closely?

options.text: Let the other driver pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the other driver pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass you. If it is safe, change lanes and allow them to go ahead. Speeding up makes it more dangerous.

questions.question: What is true about a motorcycle with a sidecar?

options.text: It can tip over if turning too fast.
It can take corners at any speed.
It should never be used to carry items.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can tip over if turning too fast.
questions.explanation: Even with three wheels on the ground, a sidecar can tip over if you turn too sharply or go too fast around a corner.

questions.question: How do many over-the-counter drugs affect riding safety?

options.text: They increase the danger of riding.
They decrease the danger of riding.
They only affect riding if you drink alcohol with them.
They affect everyone the same way.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase the danger of riding.
questions.explanation: Like alcohol, many drugs (including prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs) have side effects that can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane to be seen in the rearview mirror of the car ahead?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the center of your lane behind a car. This puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT protect you from injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: Wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Use durable materials for the best protection.
